children: Shares of Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of investment platform Groww, fell 2.5 percent in early trade on September 16 after shares worth nearly Rs 2,000 crore changed hands through block deals. Around 10.41 crore shares, equivalent to 1.69 percent of the company's equity, were sold at Rs 192 apiece in the block deal window. The transaction was valued at around Rs 1,999 crore.
Groww shares were trading at Rs 192.65 in early trade, after falling as much as 2.5 percent from their previous close of Rs 197.59. The stock had declined 1.32 percent in Tuesday's session as well.

The transaction comes after CNBC-TV18 reported on Tuesday that Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1 and Sequoia Capital Global Growth Fund III - U.S./India Annex Fund were looking to sell up to 10.02 crore shares, representing around 1.6 percent equity, in Groww through a block deal.

The proposed transaction was initially pegged at Rs 1,918.3 crore, with a floor price of Rs 191.45 per share. The floor price represented a discount of up to 3.1 percent to Groww's Tuesday closing price. The sellers were also expected to be subject to a 30-day lock-up period on any further stake sale.

The actual block deals on Wednesday were larger than the proposed transaction, both in terms of the number of shares and the total value. The 10.41 crore shares that changed hands exceeded the 10.02 crore shares indicated in the initial terms, while the transaction price of Rs 192 per share was marginally above the reported floor price of Rs 191.45.
The identities of the buyers and sellers in Wednesday's block deals were not immediately available.

The transaction marks another sizeable change in shareholding in Groww within weeks. On August 26, US venture capital firm Ribbit Capital offloaded 11.31 crore shares, equivalent to around 1.8 percent of the company's equity, through open-market transactions worth Rs 2,217.3 crore.

On the earnings front, Groww reported a 7 percent year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 735 crore for the June quarter. Revenue stood at Rs 1,501 crore, largely unchanged sequentially from Rs 1,505 crore in the March quarter. EBITDA rose 3.4 percent sequentially to Rs 970 crore from Rs 938 crore, while the EBITDA margin expanded by 230 basis points to 64.6 percent from 62.3 percent, aided by lower other expenses.

Despite the weakness over the past two sessions, Groww shares have gained 26.9 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the Nifty 50, which has declined 11.6 percent over the same period. Billionbrains Garage Ventures has a market capitalisation of around Rs 1.24 lakh crore.
